A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLEWS research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original musical-version retrieval experiments on DVI and SHS, including baseline implementations, ablations, and segment-level evaluations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds measured training and inference runtimes in Table 8.

M1.justification: The segment-distance reductions, contrastive loss, ResNet-based architecture, and training and retrieval procedures remain unchanged. The added runtime and parameter-count information does not establish a model modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use DiscogsVI-YT and SHS100k-v2 for track-level and segment-level retrieval, including best-match and random-segment protocols. The runtime analysis measures existing tasks without adding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing evaluations is unchanged. New Table 8 measures the same implemented comparison methods: CoverHunter-Coarse, CQTNet, DVINet+, ByteCover3†, and ByteCover1/2†.

E3.justification: Table 8 adds a runtime measurement protocol using one NVIDIA H100, batches of 100 audio blocks, and inference with 20-second queries, 5-second hops, Rmin, and 2,000 candidates. Existing retrieval-accuracy protocols and training schedules are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 and Table 8 examine computational cost through model sizes and training, embedding, and retrieval timings. The existing reduction and loss ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, and alternative retrieval-protocol analysis are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 3 newly identify their existing ± entries as 95% confidence intervals. The numerical intervals and uncertainty reporting elsewhere remain unchanged; no additional runs, seeds, or revised estimation procedure are reported.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds runtime results for six models. CLEWS is reported at 1.19 seconds per training batch, 40.3 milliseconds per song for embedding, and 3.5 milliseconds per retrieval query. Existing accuracy and ablation values in Tables 2–7 and all plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds asymptotic time-complexity statements for the reduction operators, including O(uv) for mean/min and O(r(uv + u + v)) for bpwr-r. The loss derivations, gradient analysis, and modified NAR definition are unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about weakly labeled segment learning, the contrastive loss, state-of-the-art retrieval, and potential applicability beyond music.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly argues that reduction sizes are small in practical use, illustrating 15 non-overlapping 20-second segments in a five-minute song. Existing interpretations of accuracy, random-segment evaluation limitations, and numerical-stability qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: The introduction replaces the anonymous placeholder with a specific sony/clews repository address for code and checkpoints. Appendix A.4 newly reports approximately two days of SHS training and nine days of DVI training on two H100-80GB GPUs. These are added disclosures, not demonstrated changes to training.

R1.justification: The cited works, background comparisons, and novelty positioning are unchanged. The concrete code link is reproducibility information rather than a new research citation.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the alignment-and-uniformity explanation, clarifies captions, and adds the short Runtime subsection in Appendix C. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 8 with parameter-count and runtime columns and expands the captions of Tables 2 and 3. Some content shifts with text reflow, but all six existing figures and the earlier table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility guidance through a concrete code/checkpoint address and training resource disclosures, while Appendix C.3 and Table 8 make computational costs assessable. The confidence-interval captions also improve clarity. These are useful, limited gains: the scientific method and accuracy evidence remain unchanged, and the runtime comparison is explicitly informal.
